import re, pathlib
changed=[]
for p in pathlib.Path('.').rglob('*.py'):
    if any(part.startswith('.') for part in p.parts): continue
    s=p.read_text(); o=s
    if p.as_posix()=='svc/api.py':
        s=re.sub(r"def legacy_fetch\(url, timeout=5\):\n    # legacy_fetch[^\n]*\n    return _get\(url, timeout\)\n\n\n","",s)
    s=re.sub(r"\blegacy_fetch\(", "fetch_v2(", s)
    s=re.sub(r"^(from svc\.api import .*)\blegacy_fetch\b", r"\1fetch_v2", s, flags=re.M)
    if s!=o: p.write_text(s); changed.append(str(p))
print(len(changed), changed)
print(read('svc/api.py'))

I removed `legacy_fetch` from `svc/api.py` and switched all its callers to `fetch_v2` with the same arguments. `fetch_v2` is now the only fetch function there. The smoke test passes, and the modules I tried import and run with the right results.

- **Call sites changed:** `svc/m00.py` through `svc/m11.py` (12 files). In the even-numbered files, `api.legacy_fetch(...)` is now `api.fetch_v2(...)`. In the odd-numbered files, the direct calls changed too.
- **Imports:** in the odd-numbered files I also had to change `from svc.api import legacy_fetch` to `import fetch_v2`. Without that, those modules would have failed to import once the function was gone.
- **Checks:** `pytest` ran 1 test and it passed. I also imported `m00`, `m01`, `m03` and `m11` directly. `m01.job_1()` returned `body:https://example.test/m01/1:9` and `m00.job_0()` returned `body:https://example.test/m00/0:5`, so the default and custom timeouts are both still passed through. I didn't import `m02` and `m04`–`m10` one by one, but they got exactly the same text change as the ones I did check.

One mention of the old name is left on purpose, because it isn't a call: the log message `LOG = "migrating callers off legacy_fetch"` in `svc/m03.py`. Say if you want it reworded.
